passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: OBJECTIVE The following discussion provides an analysis of the Company’s financial condition, cash flows and results of operations from management’s perspective and should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our objective is to also provide discussion of events and uncertainties known to management that are reasonably likely to cause reported financial information not to be indicative of future operating results or of future financial condition and to offer information that provides understanding of our financial condition, cash flows and results of operations. Refer to the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023 for additional information related to fiscal 2023. DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPANY We are a world-class food company and recognized leader in protein. Founded in 1935 by John W. Tyson, it has grown under four generations of family leadership. The Company is unified by this purpose: Tyson Foods. We Feed the World Like Family™ and has a broad portfolio of iconic products and brands including Tyson®, Jimmy Dean®, Hillshire Farm®, Ball Park®, Wright®, State Fair®, Aidells® and ibp®. Tyson Foods is dedicated to bringing high-quality food to every table in the world, safely, and affordably, now and for future generations. We operate in four reportable segments: Beef, Pork, Chicken and Prepared Foods. We measure segment profit as operating income (loss). International/Other primarily includes our foreign operations in China, Malaysia, Mexico, South Korea, Thailand and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, third-party merger and integration costs and corporate overhead related to Tyson New Ventures, LLC. For further description of the business, refer to Part I, Item 1, Business. OVERVIEW Fiscal year We utilize a 52- or 53-week accounting period ending on the Saturday closest to September 30. The Company’s accounting cycle resulted in a 52-week year for fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023. General Sales grew 2.1%, or $1.1 billion to $54.4 billion in fiscal 2025, largely due to higher average sales prices in our Beef, Pork and Prepared Foods segments, partially offset by $653 million of increased legal contingency accruals which reduced sales. We reported operating income of $1,098 million in fiscal 2025 as compared to an operating income of $1,409 million in fiscal 2024, as we experienced lower operating income in our Beef and Pork segments, partially offset by higher operating income in our Chicken and Prepared Foods segments and International/Other. In fiscal 2025, our operating income was impacted by $738 million of legal contingency accruals, $343 million of goodwill and intangible impairments, $45 million of restructuring and related charges, $41 million of charges related to a product recall and $23 million related to brand and product line discontinuations. In fiscal 2024, our results were impacted by $182 million of plant closure and disposal charges, $174 million of legal contingency accruals and $31 million of restructuring and related charges. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: These risks, which should be considered carefully with the information provided elsewhere in this report, could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. BUSINESS & OPERATIONAL RISK FACTORS We may not realize any or all of the anticipated benefits of our financial excellence programs and operational optimization plans, which may prove to be more difficult, costly or time consuming than expected. The success of our financial excellence programs or operational optimization plans, including the network optimization plan, will depend in part on our ability to successfully implement these programs and plans or any future such programs and plans in an efficient and effective manner. The implementation of financial excellence programs and operational optimization plans may be more difficult, costly, or time-consuming than expected, and may not result in any or all of the anticipated benefits. If we are unable to implement such programs or plans smoothly or successfully, or we otherwise do not realize the anticipated benefits or capture the anticipated savings, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be negatively impacted. We are subject to risks associated with our international activities, which could negatively affect our sales to customers in foreign locations, as well as our operations and assets in such locations and in the United States. In fiscal 2025, we sold products to customers in approximately 140 countries. Major sales markets include Canada, Central America, China, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Japan, Mexico, Malaysia, the Middle East, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Our sales to customers in foreign countries for fiscal 2025 totaled $7.4 billion, of which $4.8 billion related to export sales from the United States. In addition, we had approximately $0.7 billion of long-lived assets, excluding goodwill, intangibles, financial instruments and deferred tax assets, located in foreign locations, primarily Brazil, China, New Zealand, Malaysia, the Middle East and Thailand, at the end of fiscal 2025. We are subject to various risks and uncertainties relating to international sales and operations, including: closing of borders by foreign countries to the import of beef, pork and poultry products due to animal disease or other perceived health or safety issues; the impact of currency exchange rate fluctuations between the United States dollar and foreign currencies, particularly the Brazilian real, the British pound sterling, the Canadian dollar, the Chinese renminbi, the European euro, the Malaysian ringgit, the Mexican peso and the Thai baht; political and economic conditions, including ongoing conflicts and political tensions; and difficulties and costs of complying with different legal, tax and regulatory requirements impacting exports and other international activities. credit_strengths.text: Tyson's protein franchise spans beef, pork, chicken and prepared foods, and revenue has grown steadily across the three-year trend, with prepared foods and chicken offsetting weaker beef and pork results. This diversification supports cash generation through protein cycles, though operating margin remains thin relative to the staples sector median.

Operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure, leaving meaningful free cash flow that covers the dividend and reduces borrowings. Debt declined year over year as term loan repayments and maturities were retired, and the new revolver remains undrawn, providing substantial committed liquidity alongside a safe Altman zone score.

key_risks.text: Legal contingency accruals and goodwill impairments depressed reported operating income, and the risk factors flag execution risk on financial excellence and network optimization programs. If savings fail to materialize, earnings recovery stalls and leverage stays elevated relative to the sector median, leaving limited headroom before the next threshold.

The debt note shows a large senior note maturing within the next twelve months, with further maturities concentrated in the following years, so refinancing depends on continued access to investment-grade markets. Commercial paper capacity backstops short-term needs, but access could be limited or costlier, pressuring interest coverage that already trails the sector median.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is weak for the sector, with operating income covering gross interest expense only modestly, well below the staples median. Coverage should improve as legal charges lapse and chicken and prepared foods margins recover, but the cushion is thin and sensitive to beef segment losses.

Free cash flow to debt is modest and below the sector median, yet absolute free cash flow covers the dividend with room to spare, and the current ratio exceeds the sector median. Liquidity is adequate, though shareholder distributions absorb a large share of internally generated cash.

overall_credit_view.text: Net leverage sits above the sector median and the indicative financial risk profile is significant, driven by weaker cash flow to debt. Deleveraging depends on earnings recovery from depressed operating income; a modest EBITDA decline or debt increase would push leverage toward the next threshold, so the trajectory is negative-leaning absent margin improvement.

Our judgement is that Tyson retains solid access to capital markets and adequate liquidity, but thin margins, legal charges and concentrated near-term maturities keep the credit profile sensitive to protein-cycle and refinancing conditions. We would look for sustained operating income recovery and lower leverage before viewing the trend as stabilizing.

credit_strengths.text: Tyson 的蛋白質業務涵蓋牛肉、豬肉、雞肉及加工食品，且收入在三年趨勢中穩步增長，加工食品及雞肉抵銷了較弱的牛肉及豬肉業績。此多元化佈局支持蛋白質週期中的現金產生，惟營業利潤率相對必需消費品行業中位數仍然偏薄。
營運現金流充裕地支持資本開支，留下可觀的自由現金流以覆蓋股息並減少借款。債務按年下降，因定期貸款還款及到期債務已償付，且新循環信貸額度仍未提取，提供大量承諾流動性，同時 Altman 安全區評分亦屬安全。

key_risks.text: 法律或有事項計提及商譽減值壓低了報告營業收入，而風險因素亦標示財務卓越及網絡優化計劃的執行風險。若節省未能實現，盈利復甦停滯，槓桿相對行業中位數維持偏高，在下一個門檻前留下有限緩衝。
債務附註顯示一筆大額優先票據將於未來十二個月內到期，其後數年亦有進一步到期債務集中，故再融資取決於能否持續進入投資級市場。商業票據額度支持短期需要，但取用可能受限或成本更高，對已落後於行業中位數的利息覆蓋構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋對該行業而言偏弱，營業收入僅勉強覆蓋總利息支出，遠低於必需消費品中位數。隨著法律費用消退及雞肉與加工食品利潤率回升，覆蓋應會改善，但緩衝薄弱且對牛肉分部虧損敏感。
自由現金流對債務比率偏低且低於行業中位數，惟絕對自由現金流覆蓋股息仍有餘裕，且流動比率高於行業中位數。流動性充足，儘管股東分派佔內部產生現金的比例較大。

overall_credit_view.text: 淨槓桿高於行業中位數，且指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，主要受現金流對債務比率較弱所驅動。去槓桿取決於營業收入自低迷水平復甦；EBITDA 小幅下降或債務增加將把槓桿推向下一門檻，故在利潤率未改善下，軌跡偏向負面。
我們的判斷是 Tyson 仍保有穩固的資本市場准入及充足流動性，但利潤率偏薄、法律費用及近期到期債務集中，使信用狀況對蛋白質週期及再融資條件敏感。我們會尋求持續的營業收入復甦及較低槓桿，才會視趨勢為趨穩。
